items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to motor carriers of
stretch limousines
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6604

SPONSOR: SANDERS
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to motor carriers of stretch limousines

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To enhance public safety.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one adds a new subdivision 5-a to section 509-d of the Vehicle
and Traffic Law to require motor carriers to furnish the Department of
Motor Vehicles (DMV) with a list of each altered motor vehicle commonly
referred to as a "stretch limousine" designed to carry 15 or more
passengers in addition to the driver which such carrier operates if any,
and a list of all drivers such motor carrier employs who drive such
stretch limousines and whether such drivers are qualified or disquali-
fied.

Section two amends subdivision 1 of section 509-m of the Vehicle and
Traffic Law to require DMV to review the bus driver files of each driver
of a motor carrier operating stretch limousines, and annually verify
whether each such driver holds a valid driver's license valid for the
operation of a stretch limousine.

Section three adds a new subdivision 8 to section 509-m of the Vehicle
and Traffic Law to require DMV to maintain and annually update its
website to provide information regarding each motor carrier operating
stretch limousines including the carrier's name, location, address and
region of operation; whether the motor carrier is in compliance with
Article 19-A of the Vehicle and Traffic Law (Special Requirements for
Bus Drivers); the number and nature of violations of the motor carrier
resulting in convictions relating to stretch limousines; the number of
miles traveled by stretch limousines operated by the motor carrier with-
in the preceding 12 months; the total number of stretch limousine driv-
ers employed by the motor carrier, the number holding valid licenses
valid for the operation of stretch limousines and the number lacking
such license, the number disqualified, the number of convictions and
accidents involving any such driver employed by the motor carrier during
the preceding 12 months, and the number of convictions and accidents per
ten thousand miles traveled.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

The provisions of the bill pertain only to the aforementioned sections.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Following the tragic limousine crash in Schoharie, New York, in October
2018 that claimed the lives of 20 people, the worst transportation
disaster in nearly a decade, the need for updated laws governing stretch
limousines is apparent. This bill is aimed at making information on
vehicles and drivers public and easily available to consumers.

This bill will require the Department of Motor Vehicles to annually
review the driver record of persons employed by motor carriers to oper-
ate stretch limousines seating fifteen or more passengers in addition to
the driver, and annually verify whether these persons hold valid driv-
ers' licenses valid to operate stretch limousines. This bill will also
create a public database on the Department of Motor Vehicles' website,
on motor carriers of passengers which operate these stretch limousines
in New York State, in order to provide important information for consum-
er protection (e.g. company record/violations, number of miles travelled
annually, accidents, and driver licensing information). This gives the
consumer a way to check important information before hiring a company,
similar to the New York State Department of Transportation's online
database of information on commercial bus operators.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Unknown.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment
and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation
of this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and
completed on or before such effective date.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6604A

SPONSOR: SANDERS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the transportation law,
in relation to motor carriers of stretch limousines

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To enhance public safety by improving motor carrier safety data trans-
parency.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:


Section one adds a new subdivision 5-a to section 509-d of the Vehicle
and Traffic Law to require motor carriers to furnish the Department of
Motor Vehicles (DMV) with a list of each altered motor vehicle commonly
referred to as a "stretch limousine" designed to carry 10 or more
passengers in addition to the driver which such carrier operates if any,
and a list of all drivers such motor carrier employs who drive such
stretch limousines and whether such drivers are qualified or disquali-
fied.

Section two amends subdivision 1 of section 509-m of the Vehicle and
Traffic Law to require DMV to review the bus driver files of each driver
of a motor carrier operating stretch limousines, and annually verify
whether each such driver holds a valid driver's license valid for the
operation of a stretch limousine.

Section three adds a new subdivision 8 to section 509-m of the Vehicle
and Traffic Law to require DMV to maintain and annually update its
website to provide information regarding each motor carrier operating
stretch limousines including the carrier's name, location, address and
region of operation; whether the motor carrier is in compliance with
Article 19-A of the Vehicle and Traffic Law (Special Requirements for
Bus Drivers); the number and nature of violations of the motor carrier
resulting in convictions relating to stretch limousines; the number of
miles traveled by stretch limousines operated by the motor carrier with-
in the preceding 12 months; the total number of stretch limousine driv-
ers employed by the motor carrier, the number holding valid licenses
valid for the operation of stretch limousines and the number lacking
such license, the number disqualified, the number of convictions and
accidents involving any such driver employed by the motor carrier during
the preceding 12 months, and the number of convictions and accidents per
ten thousand miles traveled. To the extent the information is available,
DMV is required to provide this information on carriers with nine or
more passengers including the operator.

Section four modifies subdivision 9 of section 138 of the Transportation
Law to add the number or percentage of Class A out-of-service defects to
the existing metrics on motor carrier safety that were enacted as part
of the 2019 Adopted Budget.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

The bill expands the universe of vehicles affected to include vehicles
capable of carrying 10 or more passengers, as well as including vehicles
with nine or more to the extent the data are available, and adds the new
Section Four.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Following the tragic limousine crash in Schoharie, New York, in October
2018 that claimed the lives of 20 people, the worst transportation
disaster in nearly a decade, the need for updated laws governing stretch
limousines is apparent. This bill is aimed at making information on
vehicles and drivers public and easily available to consumers.

This bill will require the Department of Motor Vehicles to annually
review the driver record of persons employed by motor carriers to oper-
ate stretch limousines seating fifteen or more passengers in addition to
the driver, and annually verify whether these persons hold valid driv-
ers' licenses valid to operate stretch limousines.  This bill will also
create a public database on the Department of Motor Vehicles' website,
on motor carriers of passengers which operate these stretch limousines
in New York State, in order to provide important information for consum-
er protection (e.g. company record/violations, number of miles travelled
annually, accidents, and driver licensing information). This gives the
consumer a way to check important information before hiring a company,
similar to the New York State Department of Transportation's online
database of information on commercial bus operators.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019: Previous version (A.5774-A) passed Assembly on June 18.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Unknown.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment
and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation
of this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and
completed on or before such effective date.
